notes.text: Sat — That is, was settled in the house which Hiram's men had built for him, then he reflected upon the unsettled state of the ark.
Curtains — That is, in a tent or tabernacle, ver. 6, composed of several curtains.

Nathan said — Pursue thy intentions, and build an house for the ark. The design being pious and the thing not forbidden by God, Nathan hastily approves it, before he had consulted God about it, as both he and David ought to have done in a matter of so great moment. And therefore Nathan meets with this rebuke, that he is forced to acknowledge his error, and recant it. For the holy prophets did not speak all things by prophetic inspiration, but some things by an human spirit.
The word of the Lord came — Because David's mistake was pious, and from an honest mind, God would not suffer him to lie long in it.
Shalt thou — That is, thou shalt not.
Tent and tabernacle — These two seem thus to be distinguished, the one may note the curtains and hangings within, the other the frame of boards, and coverings upon it.

My servant — Lest David should be too much discouraged, or judge himself neglected of God, as one thought unworthy of so great an honour, God here gives him the honourable title of his servant, thereby signifying that he accepted of his service, and good intentions.

Appoint — That is, I will make room for them, whereas hitherto they have been much distressed by their enemies. Or, I will establish a place for them, that is, I will establish them in their place or land. My people - Among the favours which God had vouchsafed, and would vouchsafe to David, he reckons his blessings to Israel, because they were great blessings to David; partly, because the strength and happiness of a king consists in the multitude and happiness of his people; and partly, because David was a man of a public spirit, and therefore no less affected with Israel's felicity than with his own. Before time - Namely in Egypt.

And as since — Nor as they did under the Judges. But all this is to be understood with a condition, except they should notoriously forsake God. And have caused thee - That is, and as until this time in which I have given thee rest. But these words, though according to our translation they be enclosed in the same parenthesis with the foregoing clauses, may be better put without it, and taken by themselves. For the foregoing words in this verse, and in ver. 10, all concern the people of Israel; but these words concern David alone, to whom the speechs returns after a short digression concerning the people of Israel. And they may be rendered thus. And I will cause thee to rest, &c. - More fully and perfectly than yet thou dost. He will, &c. - For thy good intentions to make him an house, he will make thee an house, a sure house, that is, he will increase and uphold thy posterity, and continue thy kingdom in thy family.

Before thee — Thine eyes in some sort beholding it: for he lived to see his wise son Solomon actually placed in the throne, with reputation and general applause, which was in itself a good presage of the continuance of the kingdom in his family: and being considered, together with the infallible certainty of God's promise to him and his, (of the accomplishment whereof, this was an earnest,) gave him good assurance thereof; especially considering that he had his eyes and thoughts upon the Messiah, Psalm cx, 1, &c. whose day he saw by faith, as Abraham did, John viii, 56, and whom he knew that God would raise out of the fruit of his loins to sit on his throne, and that forever: and so the eternity of his kingdom is rightly said to be before him.

glossa.text:
*All that is in thy heart, go and do. ((RAB. in lib. Reg., tom. III.))* It is plain that the spirit of prophecy does not always irradiate the minds of the prophets. *For the Spirit breatheth where he will ((Joan. III))*. Hence Eliseus says: *The Lord hath hid it from me, and hath not told me ((IV Reg. IV))*. Which God disposes out of the dispensation of his loving-kindness: because, while he gives and withdraws the spirit of prophecy, he lifts up the minds of those who prophesy on high, and keeps them in humility, so that, receiving the spirit, they may find what they are of God, and again, not having the spirit of prophecy, they may know what they are of themselves.

((GREG., lib. VII Moral., cap. 17.)) A man ought to be clean in himself from vices, etc., *as far as* he must needs blush to instruct the minds of his neighbours.
*Shalt thou.* ((RAB.)) Another translation, etc., *as far as* he shall build me a house.
*And I will appoint a place.* He describes the time of Solomon, in which the children of Israel had peace on every side, and were not afflicted as in the time of the Judges.

*And faithful. ((RAB., ex Aug. de Civit., lib. XVII, cap. 8.))* This is truly said of Christ, etc., *as far as* the place therefore of so peaceful and secure a dwelling is eternal, where the true Israel shall be, that is, he that seeth God.

*And he sat before.* To sit before the Lord is to confess his benefits in humility.

*The law of Adam.* ((RAB.)) That is, of man, that he may serve thee in simplicity of heart and in purity, and that thou mayest do to him according to thy mercy, as thou hast done to me.

notes.text: And Mary said — Under a prophetic impulse, several things, which perhaps she herself did not then fully understand.

My spirit hath rejoiced in God my saviour — She seems to turn her thoughts here to Christ himself, who was to be born of her, as the angel had told her, he should be the Son of the Highest, whose name should be Jesus, the saviour. And she rejoiced in hope of salvation through faith in him, which is a blessing common to all true believers, more than in being his mother after the flesh, which was an honour peculiar to her. And certainly she had the same reason to rejoice in God her saviour hat we have: because he had regarded the low estate of his handmaid, in like manner as he regarded our low estate; and vouchsafed to come and save her and us, when we were reduced to the lowest estate of sin and misery.

He hath wrought strength with his arm — That is, he hath shown the exceeding greatness of his power. She speaks prophetically of those things as already done, which God was about to do by the Messiah. He hath scattered the proud - Visible and invisible.
He hath put down the mighty — Both angels and men.
He hath helped his servant Israel — By sending the Messiah.
To his seed — His spiritual seed: all true believers.

glossa.text: *My soul doth magnify the Lord. ((ID.))* First she professes the gifts spiritually granted to her, etc., *as far as* I spend in the keeping of his commandments.

*And hath exulted. ((ID.)) ((ID.))* Because I do not care for earthly things, prosperity does not soften me, adversity does not break me, but the memory of him alone delights me, from whom eternal salvation is hoped for; I rejoice in the Godhead of him by whose conception in time my flesh is made fruitful.

*Because he hath regarded. ((ID.))* Behold how lowly are the things she feels concerning herself, etc., *as far as* and out of the small and the weak he makes them great and strong.

*Because he hath done great things to me.* Because in me he took flesh, and cleansed me from sins, and conferred upon me the gifts of the Holy Ghost.

 *And mercy. ((BEDA.))* From the special gifts she turns herself to the general judgments of God, etc., *as far as* he adds what the despisers deserve.

*He hath filled the hungry with good things. ((ID.))* They who desire eternal things with all zeal; shall be filled, when Christ shall have appeared in glory. But they who rejoice in earthly things are sent away at the last empty of all blessedness. In the present life also we see the humble filled with divine grace, and the proud deprived of the light of truth.

*As he spoke to our fathers.* Making mention of the fathers to whom this salvation was revealed, she names Abraham expressly, to whom the incarnation itself was first made manifest. *And to his seed for ever.* Not so much to those born of the flesh as to those who have followed the footsteps of faith, to whom the coming of the Saviour was promised for ever, because the promise of the inheritance itself shall be closed by no end. For both unto the end of the world believers shall not be lacking, and the glory of blessedness shall be everlasting.

notes.text: Now to him who is able — The last words of this epistle exactly answer the first, chapter i, 1-v, chap. i, 1-v, in particular, concerning the power of God, the gospel, Jesus Christ, the scriptures, the obedience of faith, all nations. To establish you - Both Jews and gentiles. According to my gospel, and the preaching of Jesus Christ - That is, according to the tenor of the gospel of Jesus Christ, which I preach. According to the Revelation of the mystery - Of the calling of the gentiles, which, as plainly as it was foretold in the Prophets, was still hid from many even of the believing Jews.

According to the commandment — The foundation of the apostolical office. Of the eternal God - A more proper epithet could not be. A new dispensation infers no change in God. Known unto him are all his works, and every variation of them, from eternity. Made known to all nations - Not barely that they might know, but enjoy it also, through obeying the faith.

To the only wise God — Whose manifold wisdom is known in the church through the gospel, Eph. iii, 10. "To him who is able," and, to the wise God," are joined, as 1 Cor. i, 24, where Christ is styled "the wisdom of God," and "the power of God." To him be glory through Christ Jesus forever - And let every believer say, Amen!

glossa.text:
*Now to him.* Thus do I admonish you. But to him who is able to confirm you be glory, from whom alone, being good, are all good things; wherein the sum of the epistle is noted, because here the Apostle principally purposes to admonish them that they attribute all things to the grace of God.

*According to the revelation.* By *mystery* he means the incarnation of Christ, etc., which things were hidden from eternal times: because although in some part they had been known to the ancient fathers, yet by none were they fully known, until in their own time they were revealed through Christ himself.

*By the Scriptures of the prophets.* Unlocked by him, giving testimony to this preaching. *Made manifest* among all nations unto obedience, that is, that they may obey the faith by working well. *Kept silent* to others, but known to God alone: because although it be now revealed to men, yet it is known to God alone, because he alone knows why it was so done. Wherein he restrains the inquirers who ask: why has God deferred so long? why has he permitted so many nations to perish.
*To whom be honor. ((AUG.))* That which is added: To whom be glory, etc., *as far as* because through him God the Trinity became known to men, which is the mystery.

notes.text: In the sixth month — After Elisabeth had conceived.

Espoused — It was customary among the Jews, for persons that married to contract before witnesses some time before. And as Christ was to be born of a pure virgin, so the wisdom of God ordered it to be of one espoused, that to prevent reproach he might have a reputed father, according to the flesh.

Hail, thou highly favoured; the Lord is with thee; blessed art thou among women — Hail is the salutation used by our Lord to the women after his resurrection: thou art highly favoured, or hast found favour with God, ver. 30, is no more than was said of Noah, Moses, and David. The Lord is with thee, was said to Gideon, Judg. vi, 12; and blessed shall she be above women, of Jael, Judg. v, 24. This salutation gives no room for any pretense of paying adoration to the virgin; as having no appearance of a prayer, or of worship offered to her.

He shall be called the Son of the Highest — In this respect also: and that in a more eminent sense than any, either man or angel, can be called so. The Lord shall give him the throne of his father David - That is, the spiritual kingdom, of which David's was a type.
He shall reign over the house of Jacob — In which all true believers are included.

The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee — The power of God was put forth by the Holy Ghost, as the immediate Divine agent in this work: and so he exerted the power of the Highest as his own power, who together with the Father and the Son is the most high God. Therefore also - Not only as he is God from eternity, but on this account likewise he shall be called the Son of God.

And behold, thy cousin Elisabeth — Though Elisabeth was of the house of Aaron, and Mary of the house of David, by the fathers side, they might be related by their mothers. For the law only forbad heiresses marrying into another tribe. And so other persons continually intermarried; particularly the families of David and of Levi.
And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord — It is not improbable, that this time of the virgin's humble faith, consent, and expectation, might be the very time of her conceiving.

glossa.text:
*And in the sixth month. ((HIER.))* As in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God into a city of Galilee, so in the sixth millennium Christ was sent,

*Gabriel. ((BEDA.))* For this reason angels are sometimes marked out by a name, so that from the name itself it may be shown what they come to minister. Gabriel is the strength of God, because he announces him who was coming to war down the devil.
*To a virgin.* A woman seduced by the devil brought in death: on the contrary, a woman taught by an angel brought forth salvation.

*The Lord is with thee.* Whom by a new love of chastity he raised up to heavenly things, and afterwards, human nature mediating, consecrated with all the fullness of the Godhead. *Blessed art thou among women.* Who, without example in the condition of women, is both virgin and mother, and brought forth God.
*She was troubled,* etc. Because she did not know whether what the angel said was past or to come.

*And the angel said to her: Fear not, Mary.* Her, troubled by the unwonted salutation, he calls by name as one more familiarly known. He bids her not to fear, and more fully explains why he had called her full of grace.

*Jesus.* Jesus is called saviour, or salutary. For he himself shall save, not the people of Israel, but his own people, whether from the uncircumcision or from the circumcision, gathered into one fold under one shepherd.
*The throne of David his father. ((BEDA.))* That is, the Israelite people, etc., *as far as* in those who, cut from the wild olive, have been grafted into the good olive.

*The Holy One shall be called the Son of God.* Jesus is born holy, who was to overcome the condition of corruptible nature, and he was not conceived by the mingling of carnal union. We, bound fast by the condition of corruptible nature, can be sanctified through grace. And it is fitting that she who conceived as a virgin against custom should bring forth the Son of God above the custom of human usage.

*And behold,* etc. ((BEDA.)) Lest the virgin should despair of the childbearing, etc., *as far as* she might know that the forerunner too was to be born of a barren old woman.

*Thy cousin.* Because she was of the tribe of Levi, that is, of the tribe of God.

((BEDA.)) We read that Aaron, who was of the tribe of Levi, etc., *as far as* which according to God did not lack the fellowship of a spiritual kinship.

*Behold the handmaid of the Lord.* She does not exalt herself for the singularity of her merit, but, mindful in all things of her own condition and of the divine kinship, she confesses herself to be the handmaid of him whose mother she is chosen to be, and with great devotion desires the angel's promise to be fulfilled.

echoes.text: Hannah prayed, and said: “My heart exults in Yahweh! My horn is exalted in Yahweh. My mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.
echoes.note: The Magnificat's opening, 'My soul magnifies the Lord, my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,' is modeled directly on Hannah's Song: 'My heart exults in the Lord... I rejoice in your salvation' (1 Samuel 2:1). Hannah's hymn is the structural template for the whole canticle; high volume and strong recurrence.

echoes.text: She vowed a vow, and said, “Yahweh of Armies, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your handmaid, and remember me, and not forget your handmaid, but will give to your handmaid a boy, then I will give him to Yahweh all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
echoes.note: 'He has looked at the humble state (tapeinosin) of his handmaid' quotes Hannah's prayer that God would 'look on the affliction (tapeinosin) of your handmaid' (1 Samuel 1:11 LXX). The shared rare-noun + handmaid combination is high-volume and ties the canticle's singer to Hannah.

echoes.text: Leah said, “Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy.” She named him Asher.
echoes.note: 'From now on, all generations will call me blessed' takes up Leah's 'the women will call me blessed' (Genesis 30:13 LXX), spoken at the birth of a son. The call-me-blessed formula is distinctive matriarchal speech, here universalized to all generations.

echoes.text: He has sent redemption to his people. He has ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awesome!
echoes.note: 'Holy is his name' quotes Psalm 111:9, 'holy and awesome is his name' (cf. Psalm 99:3). The fixed liturgical predication of the divine name gives high volume; Psalm 111 also feeds the Benedictus (1:68), showing recurrence.

echoes.text: But Yahweh’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with those who fear him, his righteousness to children’s children;
echoes.note: 'His mercy is for generations of generations on those who fear him' quotes Psalm 103:17, 'the steadfast love of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him.' The mercy + on-those-who-fear-him + perpetual-generations combination is high-volume and distinctive.

echoes.text: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
echoes.note: 'My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior' closely matches 'I will rejoice in the Lord; I will take joy in the God of my salvation' (Habakkuk 3:18 LXX). The rejoice-in-God-my-savior formula is distinctive and reinforces the exultant-prophetic-hymn register.

echoes.text: My soul shall be joyful in Yahweh. It shall rejoice in his salvation.
echoes.note: 'My soul shall rejoice in the Lord, exulting in his salvation' (Psalm 35:9) supplies the soul-rejoices-in-salvation diction underlying 1:47. A coherent psalmic echo within the cluster of rejoicing-in-God's-deliverance texts.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: 'My soul shall exult in my God' (Isaiah 61:10) within the Spirit-anointed-good-news passage contributes to the rejoicing diction of the canticle's opening. Thematic coherence with eschatological salvation supports the echo.

echoes.text: Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she said, “Because Yahweh has looked at my affliction. For now my husband will love me.”
echoes.note: 'He has looked at the humble state' also echoes Leah's 'the Lord has looked upon my affliction' at Reuben's birth (Genesis 29:32 LXX). The look-on-affliction-of-the-lowly motif coheres with the matriarchal reversal theme; a supporting echo to the Hannah primary.

echoes.text: Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then they said among the nations, “Yahweh has done great things for them.” Yahweh has done great things for us, and we are glad.
echoes.note: 'He who is mighty has done great things for me' echoes 'The Lord has done great things for us; we are glad' (Psalm 126:2-3). The great-things-the-Lord-has-done formula is a coherent psalmic source for the canticle's praise.

echoes.text: He is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things, which your eyes have seen.
echoes.note: 'He... has done great things for me' also recalls 'He is your praise; he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things' (Deuteronomy 10:21). A further great-deeds source coherent with the doxological tone.

echoes.text: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
echoes.note: 'His mercy is for generations... on those who fear him' echoes the Decalogue's promise of steadfast love 'to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments' (Exodus 20:6; Deuteronomy 5:10). The covenant mercy-to-generations formula coheres with Psalm 103.

echoes.text: You have broken Rahab in pieces, like one of the slain. You have scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.
echoes.note: 'He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered the proud' echoes Psalm 89:10, 'you scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.' The arm + scatter combination is distinctive, and Psalm 89 (Davidic covenant) coheres with the chapter's throne themes; high volume.

echoes.text: “Talk no more so exceeding proudly. Don’t let arrogance come out of your mouth, For Yahweh is a God of knowledge. By him actions are weighed. “The bows of the mighty men are broken. Those who stumbled are armed with strength.
echoes.note: 'He has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts' draws on Hannah's warning, 'Talk no more so very proudly... the bows of the mighty are broken' (1 Samuel 2:3-4). The humbling-of-the-arrogant motif is structurally central to Hannah's Song, the canticle's master text.

echoes.text: Yahweh makes poor, and makes rich. He brings low, he also lifts up. He raises up the poor out of the dust. He lifts up the needy from the dunghill, To make them sit with princes, and inherit the throne of glory. For the pillars of the earth are Yahweh’s. He has set the world on them.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly' directly reworks Hannah: 'The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and he exalts. He raises up the poor from the dust... to make them sit with princes' (1 Samuel 2:7-8). High volume; the great-reversal heart of the Magnificat.

echoes.text: Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread. Those who were hungry are satisfied. Yes, the barren has borne seven. She who has many children languishes.
echoes.note: 'He has filled the hungry with good things. He has sent the rich away empty' reworks Hannah's 'those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, but the hungry have ceased to hunger' (1 Samuel 2:5). The hungry-filled / sated-emptied antithesis is high-volume and distinctive.

echoes.text: For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good.
echoes.note: 'He has filled the hungry with good things' quotes Psalm 107:9, 'he satisfies the longing soul, and the hungry soul he fills with good things.' Near-verbatim; a strong psalmic doublet to the Hannah hunger-reversal.

echoes.text: He raises up the poor out of the dust. Lifts up the needy from the ash heap; that he may set him with princes, even with the princes of his people.
echoes.note: 'Has exalted the lowly' reflects Psalm 113:7-8, 'He raises the poor from the dust... to make them sit with princes.' Psalm 113 (a Hallel psalm) shares both the lifting-the-lowly motif and its own debt to Hannah; high volume within the reversal cluster.

echoes.text: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend, You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;’
echoes.note: 'He has given help to Israel, his servant' draws on Isaiah 41:8-9, 'But you, Israel, my servant... whom I have taken... I have chosen you and not cast you off.' The Israel-my-servant designation plus God's helping/upholding (Isaiah 41:10) gives high volume for the canticle's turn to corporate Israel.

echoes.text: He has remembered his loving kindness and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
echoes.note: 'That he might remember mercy' quotes Psalm 98:3, 'He has remembered his steadfast love and faithfulness to the house of Israel.' The remembered-mercy-to-Israel formula is distinctive and rounds off the canticle's covenant-faithfulness theme.

echoes.text: You will give truth to Jacob, and mercy to Abraham, as you have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.
echoes.note: 'As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his seed forever' echoes Micah 7:20, 'You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as you have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.' The mercy-to-Abraham-as-sworn-to-the-fathers structure is high-volume and concludes both hymns (cf. 1:73).

echoes.text: I will establish my covenant between me and you and your seed after you throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to you and to your seed after you.
echoes.note: 'To Abraham and his seed forever' takes up the Abrahamic covenant, 'to be God to you and to your offspring after you... an everlasting covenant' (Genesis 17:7; cf. 13:15). The to-Abraham-and-his-seed-forever formula is distinctive covenant language; high volume.

echoes.text: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones' echoes Job 12:19, 'he leads priests away stripped and overthrows the mighty.' Job 12's catalogue of God's reversal of the powerful (12:14-25) coheres with the Magnificat's social inversion; a focused supporting allusion.

echoes.text: The Lord cast down the thrones of rulers, And set the meek in their stead.
echoes.note: 'He has put down princes from their thrones' closely matches Sirach 10:14, 'The Lord has cast down the thrones of rulers, and has seated the lowly in their place.' A deuterocanonical near-parallel with the throne-down / lowly-up structure; strong coherence, moderate independent volume.

echoes.text: thus says the Lord Yahweh: Remove the turban, and take off the crown; this will not be as it was; exalt that which is low, and abase that which is high.
echoes.note: 'Put down princes from their thrones... exalted the lowly' echoes Ezekiel 21:26, 'exalt that which is low, and abase that which is high.' The abase-the-high / exalt-the-low formula coheres with the inversion theme as a prophetic supporting echo.

echoes.text: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your seed greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your seed will possess the gate of his enemies.
echoes.note: 'And his seed forever' also recalls the oath at the Aqedah, 'I will surely multiply your offspring' (Genesis 22:17), the same sworn promise the Benedictus names explicitly at 1:73. A coherent supporting echo binding Magnificat and Benedictus.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s ark remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months: and Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom, and all his house.
echoes.note: 'Mary stayed with her about three months' parallels the ark of God remaining 'in the house of Obed-edom... three months' (2 Samuel 6:11). Combined with the ark allusions of 1:43-44, the three-month notice supports the Mary-as-ark typology; figural and contested.

harmony.title: The Visitation (Magnificat)
harmony.note: Mary's song — "he has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly."

echoes.text: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
echoes.note: A 'virgin' (parthenos) of the house of David who will 'conceive... and give birth to a son' and name him directly evokes Isaiah 7:13-14 (LXX), 'the virgin shall conceive and bear a son.' The house-of-David setting plus virgin + conceive + bear + name a son yields high volume and is the controlling messianic citation.

echoes.text: “Jael shall be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed shall she be above women in the tent.
echoes.note: 'Blessed are you among women' quotes the blessing of Jael, 'Most blessed of women be Jael' (Judges 5:24). The exact superlative-blessing-of-a-woman formula gives high volume; it recurs on Elizabeth's lips at 1:42.

echoes.text: Ozias said to her, “Blessed are you, daughter, in the sight of the Most High God, above all the women upon the earth; and blessed is the Lord God, who created the heavens and the earth, who directed you to cut off the head of the prince of our enemies.
echoes.note: Uzziah blesses Judith, 'Blessed are you... above all women on earth' (Judith 13:18), the closest verbal and contextual parallel to the angel/Elizabeth's beatitude over Mary. A deuterocanonical text celebrating a woman through whom God delivers Israel; high distinctiveness.

echoes.text: When your days are fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, who shall proceed out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men; but my loving kindness shall not […]
echoes.note: 'The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign... forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom' is built on the Davidic covenant of 2 Samuel 7:12-16, where God establishes David's offspring and 'his throne forever.' High volume (throne, forever, kingdom, father David) and the foundational role of Nathan's oracle make this the primary source.

echoes.text: For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on the throne of David, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.
echoes.note: 'The throne of his father David... no end to his Kingdom' closely echoes Isaiah 9:7, 'of the increase of his government and of peace there will be no end, on the throne of David.' The 'no end' phrase is distinctive and reinforces the messianic-throne reading alongside 2 Samuel 7.

echoes.text: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one, I have sworn to David, my servant, ‘I will establish your seed forever, and build up your throne to all generations.’” Selah.
echoes.note: The everlasting Davidic throne is celebrated in Psalm 89:3-4,29,36, 'I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations.' Recurrence of the throne-forever covenant language across this Psalm supports the high-volume Davidic cluster here.

echoes.text: yes, while I was speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening offering.
echoes.note: 'The angel Gabriel was sent from God' continues the Danielic Gabriel motif (Daniel 8:16; 9:21), where the same angel is 'sent' to deliver revelation. Recurrence within the chapter, more than fresh volume here, secures the allusion.

echoes.text: Sing, daughter of Zion! Shout, Israel! Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem. Yahweh has taken away your judgments. He has thrown out your enemy. The King of Israel, Yahweh, is in your midst. You will not be afraid of evil any more. In that day, it will be said to Jerusalem, “Don’t be afraid, Zion. Don’t let your hands be weak.” Yahweh, your God, is in your midst, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He […]
echoes.note: 'Rejoice (chaire)... the Lord is with you' echoes the address to Daughter Zion: 'Rejoice, O Daughter of Zion... the Lord your God is in your midst' (Zephaniah 3:14-17 LXX). The greeting-rejoice + indwelling-Lord pairing casts Mary figurally as Zion; volume is moderate but coherence strong.

echoes.text: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your King comes to you! He is righteous, and having salvation; lowly, and riding on a donkey, even on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
echoes.note: 'Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion' announcing the coming king (Zechariah 9:9) is a second Daughter-Zion 'rejoice' source standing behind Gabriel's chaire. The royal-advent context coheres with the Davidic throne promise that follows; the link competes with Zephaniah 3 and is thus contested.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s angel appeared to him, and said to him, “Yahweh is with you, you mighty man of valor!”
echoes.note: 'The Lord is with you' reproduces the angel's salutation to Gideon, 'The Lord is with you, mighty man of valor' (Judges 6:12), within a near-identical commissioning-of-a-deliverer scene including a 'how can this be' objection. The shared formula and scene-type give a coherent allusion.

echoes.text: But Noah found favor in Yahweh’s eyes.
echoes.note: 'You have found favor with God' uses the Septuagintal idiom of Noah, who 'found favor in the eyes of the Lord' (Genesis 6:8; cf. Exodus 33:17 of Moses). The found-favor formula marks Mary as a chosen recipient of divine grace in the line of Israel's elect.

echoes.text: There was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
echoes.note: 'There will be no end to his Kingdom' resonates with the Son of Man's 'everlasting dominion which shall not pass away, and his kingdom one that shall not be destroyed' (Daniel 7:14). The everlasting, indestructible kingdom motif coheres with the Danielic frame already established by Gabriel.

echoes.text: and I will make that which was lame a remnant, and that which was cast far off a strong nation: and Yahweh will reign over them on Mount Zion from then on, even forever.”
echoes.note: 'He will reign over the house of Jacob forever' faintly echoes 'the Lord will reign over them in Mount Zion... forever' (Micah 4:7). The everlasting-reign-over-restored-Israel idea coheres, but the diction is generic and the Davidic sources above are nearer, so this is a low, contested echo.

echoes.text: Moses wasn’t able to enter into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle.
echoes.note: 'The power of the Most High will overshadow (episkiasei) you' uses the verb for the glory-cloud that 'overshadowed' the tent of meeting when the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle (Exodus 40:35 LXX). The distinctive Shekinah-overshadowing diction frames Mary as the dwelling place of God's presence; high volume.

echoes.text: Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes round, and Sarah will have a son.”
echoes.note: 'For everything spoken by God is possible' answers the rhetorical question to Abraham and Sarah, 'Is anything too hard (impossible, LXX) for the Lord?' (Genesis 18:14), in the very context of a miraculous conception by an old, barren woman. The verbal and situational match is high-volume and pointed.

echoes.text: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
echoes.note: 'The Holy Spirit will come on you' may echo the Spirit of God hovering over the waters at creation (Genesis 1:2), framing the conception as a new creative act. Thematic coherence is suggestive but verbal overlap is thin, so the link is a contested creation-echo.

echoes.text: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
echoes.note: 'The holy one who is born from you will be called the Son of God' draws on the Davidic adoption formula, 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son' (2 Samuel 7:14). Coheres tightly with the throne-of-David promise of 1:32-33, extending the Nathan-oracle source.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: 'Son of God' applied to the messianic king recalls 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you' (Psalm 2:7). The royal son-of-God theme coheres, but the title is mediated through 2 Samuel 7 and is conventional, so Psalm 2 is a contested secondary echo.

echoes.text: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age. Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
echoes.note: 'Elizabeth your relative also has conceived a son in her old age... who was called barren' replays the Sarah situation of Genesis 18:11 and the impossible-birth promise. Recurrence of the aged-barren-woman motif (cf. 1:7) sets up the 'nothing impossible' declaration that follows.

echoes.text: Ah Lord Yahweh! Behold, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm; there is nothing too hard for you,
echoes.note: 'Nothing will be impossible with God' also echoes Jeremiah 32:17,27, 'Ah, Lord God!... nothing is too hard for you... is anything too hard for me?' The omnipotence formula reinforces the Genesis 18 source with a prophetic doublet.

echoes.text: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
echoes.note: Job's confession, 'I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be thwarted' (Job 42:2 LXX), is a further scriptural articulation of the impossibility-with-God theme Gabriel invokes. A coherent supporting echo of divine omnipotence.

echoes.text: She vowed a vow, and said, “Yahweh of Armies, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your handmaid, and remember me, and not forget your handmaid, but will give to your handmaid a boy, then I will give him to Yahweh all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
echoes.note: 'Behold, the handmaid (doule) of the Lord' takes up Hannah's self-designation as 'your handmaid' before the Lord (1 Samuel 1:11). The humble servant-woman posture coheres with the Hannah/Magnificat substratum that crystallizes a few verses later.

registers.label: Spare
lines: My soul magnifies the Lord.
My spirit rejoices in God my Savior.
He has scattered the proud, brought down the mighty.
He has lifted the lowly and filled the hungry.
The angel said: nothing is impossible with God.
Here we are; let it be to us as you say.
Come, let us worship the One who keeps his promise.
Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The angel came to a girl in Nazareth and named her favored; she was troubled, and she listened, and at last she said yes.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
For nothing is impossible with God — the barren conceive, the lowly are lifted, the hungry sit down to a full table.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
My soul magnifies the Lord, she sang; he has remembered his mercy from age to age.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
So we open our hands like Mary and answer the God who comes to us: let it be.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The angel comes to Mary with impossible news.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
The proud are scattered, the lowly lifted high.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
She opens her hands and answers: let it be.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Come, let us worship and say our own yes.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.
